ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Jacqueline du Pré

code.originalText: Six months: first 600 mg dose of ocrelizumab, no evidence of disease activity, immunoglobulins, vaccination response, pregnancy planning and her return to performing

text.paragraph: Six months: first 600 mg dose of ocrelizumab. [S]

Ms. du Pré comes on the day of her first 600 mg dose of ocrelizumab, six months after starting treatment. She has had no relapse and no new symptoms. She played chamber music in public in August and last month, has a concerto booked for the spring, and gives master classes at a conservatory twice a month. Faint tingling in the left fingertips comes only after long practice. Fatigue is manageable with swimming and an after-lunch rest. She had influenza and COVID-19 vaccines a month ago. She asked when it would be safe to try for a baby, perhaps in a year or two. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-12; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Vibration slightly reduced in the left fingertips only; otherwise normal. Nine-hole peg test 18.5 seconds right, 19.5 seconds left. EDSS 1.0

Numbness, tingling and loss of position sense in the fingers of both hands for three weeks, worse on the left, with clumsiness that makes her lose her place on the fingerboard, an electric feeling down the spine on bending the neck (Lhermitte's sign), and fatigue; a similar month of tingling in the fingers 18 months ago settled on its own. A lesion of the cervical spinal cord must be found: MRI of the brain and spine with contrast booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented loss of sensation in her fingers and fatigue. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, active: a current relapse (partial cervical myelitis at C3 to C4 with sensory loss and clumsiness of the hands) after an earlier sensory episode; dissemination in space and time on MRI, with an enhancing cord lesion and an enhancing brain lesion; CSF-specific oligoclonal bands; aquaporin-4 antibody negative; meets the 2017 McDonald criteria and the 2024 revision; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented diagnosis
S — Synthetic course, imaging and laboratory detail; linked to her documented diagnosis in October 1973.
Vitamin D deficiency: 25-hydroxyvitamin D 16 ng/mL; replacement to correct the deficiency, not as a treatment for multiple sclerosis

Acute uncomplicated cystitis (Escherichia coli) seven weeks after the first ocrelizumab course, with a pseudo-relapse: two days of returning tingling in the fingers with a low fever and no new neurological deficit; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent infection; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, on ocrelizumab (G35.A). No evidence of disease activity at six months: no relapse, no new or enhancing lesions on the re-baseline MRI, and stable examination (EDSS 1.0, nine-hole peg 18.5 and 19.5 seconds). IgG 930 mg/dL is normal and IgM 46 mg/dL is low-normal, as is common on anti-CD20 therapy. Hepatitis B surface antibody is 6 mIU/mL after two doses, not protective, because the second dose came after B-cell depletion. Pregnancy: ocrelizumab does not need to be stopped long in advance; the usual plan is to try to conceive a few months after a dose, stopping contraception at that point, and to restart treatment after delivery; breastfeeding is possible. [S]
Ocrelizumab 600 mg today, then every six months.
Blood count and immunoglobulins before each dose; MRI of the brain yearly.
Hepatitis B: counsel on avoiding exposure; a booster is unlikely to work while B cells are depleted, so it is deferred and the antibody rechecked if treatment changes.
Preconception visit with the neurologist when she is ready.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). 38 ng/mL on cholecalciferol. [S]
Continue cholecalciferol 4000 units daily.
